primary_claim: SHIFT's validation on the Bias in Bios de-biasing task is confounded: the same de-biasing can be achieved almost as well by ablating only 10 post-embedding SAE latents (rather than the original 55) or even without any SAEs at all, by simply removing gender-related tokens and training an unbiased probe, undermining Bias in Bios as a meaningful test bed for SHIFT/SAE downstream utility.

effect.metric: out-of-sample / worst-group accuracy of de-biased Bias in Bios probe
effect.value: ablating only 10 embedding SAE latents: 85.6% OOS / 72.3% worst-group (vs. 88.5% / 76% for the original 55-feature ablation); removing gender-related tokens with no SAEs at all: 93.7% OOS / 89.2% worst-group

contradicts_or_qualifies: Marks et al. 2024 validate SHIFT on the Bias in Bios task and argue this demonstrates real-world downstream utility of SAEs; this post shows the same de-biasing can be matched or exceeded by ablating just 10 embedding-layer SAE latents or by removing gender-related tokens without any SAE/language model at all, suggesting Bias in Bios is too simple a test bed to validate SHIFT or SAE utility
stated_future_work: use SHIFT to build a better deception probe in Goldowsky-Dill et al. (2025)'s setting as conclusive proof that SHIFT (and SAEs) are useful in downstream tasks
use SAEs to find the most impactful features in reward models and ablate/scale down irrelevant features to obtain less sycophantic models
apply SHIFT to distinguish between regular models and model organisms of misaligned AI, such as reward hackers or situationally aware models that act differently during deployment
benchmark SHIFT's performance against other DBIC tools such as linear probes and crosscoder-based model diffing approaches
focus more on what safety-relevant concepts to disentangle (e.g. doing what the human wants vs. doing what looks good), not just how well a method can disentangle arbitrary concept pairs
limitations_stated: this doc primarily focuses on the v2 version of the Marks et al. 2024 paper and only on results on pythia-70m-deduped, though the authors believe the critique extends to Gemma-2 2b
results were collected informally across a scattered collection of distinct Colab notebooks found in December and not shared until now
follow-up SHIFT-like studies still focus on fairly toy settings; the authors are not aware of research disentangling safety-relevant concepts specifically
quote: if you only ablate the 10 features in the post-embedding SAE, the resulting probe achieves an out-of-sample accuracy of 85.6% (compared to 88.5% after ablating 55 features)
